mainTopic: How קדשי מזבח and קדשי בדק הבית differ: which offerings make a תמורה, paying craftsmen, unspecified consecrations, and מעילה on by-products
overview: The משנה finishes its list of laws that apply only to קדשי מזבח, such as offspring and milk staying forbidden after פדיון. It then lists laws that apply only to קדשי בדק הבית. The גמרא tests the משנה's rule that all קדשי מזבח make a תמורה, using birds, a ולד, and a תמורה itself. It concludes that the rule covers only the main animal offering, so the משנה can follow even the רבנן. רבי אבהו learns from "ועשו לי" that craftsmen may be paid from בדק הבית funds. The גמרא shows that the rule 'unspecified consecrations go to בדק הבית' does not follow רבי יהושע. It brings two versions of רב's explanation of the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע, which turns on whether a person splits his vow. Finally, 'takes effect on everything' is shown to include shavings and leaves. A ברייתא teaches that milk and eggs carry מעילה only for בדק הבית, not for altar animals.

steps.title: More laws of altar animals that do not apply to Temple maintenance property
steps.stepSummary: The משנה continues its list of laws unique to קדשי מזבח. Their offspring and milk stay forbidden even after פדיון. Slaughtering them outside the עזרה brings liability. They are not used to pay craftsmen. None of this is true of קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Their offspring and their milk are forbidden after they are redeemed. Someone who slaughters them outside the Temple is liable. We do not pay craftsmen their wages from them. None of this is true of items consecrated for Temple maintenance.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing its list of rules that apply only to animals set aside for the altar. It ends by saying none of these rules apply to Temple maintenance property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after a blemished altar animal is redeemed, some of its holiness stays: its milk remains forbidden, and so does its offspring if it was conceived before the פדיון and born after it. Rashi: an offspring conceived after the פדיון is permitted. It is also so holy that slaughtering it outside the עזרה is a real sin, and it cannot be used as ordinary payment. קדשי בדק הבית only have monetary holiness, so none of these laws apply to them.

keyTerms.meaning: Items consecrated to be offered on the altar
Items consecrated for the upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש, holy only for their value
Redemption: buying back a consecrated item so the holiness moves onto money
Slaughtering an offering outside the Temple courtyard, which is forbidden
Craftsmen who work in the Temple

phrases.english: Their offspring and their milk
are forbidden after their redemption
phrases.notes: This means an altar animal that got a blemish and was redeemed, and then gave birth or gave milk.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָה שֶׁאֵין כֵּן בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list, which began on the previous page
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Offspring and milk of קדשי מזבח stay forbidden after פדיון. Slaughtering them outside brings liability. They may not be used to pay craftsmen. None of this applies to קדשי בדק הבית.

steps.title: Laws that apply only to Temple maintenance property
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists four ways that קדשי בדק הבית are stricter or broader than קדשי מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are rules that apply to Temple maintenance property but not to altar offerings. An unspecified consecration goes to Temple maintenance. Consecrating for Temple maintenance works on anything. One is liable for מעילה even on what grows from it. The owners get no benefit from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now flips sides and lists the rules that apply only to Temple maintenance property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone says 'this is הקדש' without saying what for, it goes to בדק הבית. Anything at all can be consecrated for בדק הבית, even things that could never go on the altar. מעילה applies even to by-products such as milk or eggs. Unlike a שלמים, whose meat the owner eats, the owner gets nothing from בדק הבית property.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrations made without saying their purpose
Takes effect on everything, any kind of item
One is liable for מעילה, the misuse of consecrated property
By-products or growths, such as milk, wool or eggs
Benefit for the owners

steps.whatToRemember: קדשי מזבח have bodily holiness, so their laws follow them even after פדיון. קדשי בדק הבית are holy for their value, but they cover everything, including by-products, and leave nothing for the owner.

phrases.english: There is something in items consecrated for Temple maintenance
phrases.notes: He means: there are rules here that do not apply to altar offerings.

phrases.english: that unspecified consecrations go to Temple maintenance

phrases.english: consecration for Temple maintenance takes effect on everything
and one is liable for misuse of what grows from them
and there is no benefit in them for the owners

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to the other side of the comparison: what is unique to בדק הבית
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unspecified consecrations go to בדק הבית. It takes effect on everything. מעילה applies to its by-products. The owners get no benefit from it.

steps.title: Birds are altar offerings, yet they make no substitute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that all קדשי מזבח make a תמורה. Another משנה teaches that birds and מנחות do not make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really a rule that everything consecrated for the altar makes a substitute? Birds are altar offerings, and we learned that meal offerings and birds do not make a substitute!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It attacks the משנה's general statement that every altar offering can make a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in our משנה, one of the laws listed for קדשי מזבח was that they make a תמורה. But bird offerings are clearly קדשי מזבח, and a different משנה says they do not make a תמורה. So the rule seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: A general rule
A substitute: an animal someone tries to exchange for a consecrated one, which then becomes holy too
Bird offerings: turtledoves and young pigeons
Meal offerings made of flour

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is questioning whether birds are קדשי מזבח. They clearly are. The question is only whether the rule 'all קדשי מזבח make a תמורה' covers them.

phrases.english: Gemara
And is it a general rule
that everything consecrated for the altar makes a substitute?
phrases.notes: This is quoting the earlier part of our משנה, on the previous page.

phrases.english: But there are birds
which are consecrated for the altar
and we learned
meal offerings and birds do not make a substitute

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְלָלָא הוּא דְּכׇל קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ עוֹשִׂין תְּמוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a challenge to the משנה's list
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that all קדשי מזבח make a תמורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Birds are קדשי מזבח, but another משנה says they do not make a תמורה. So the rule cannot cover all קדשי מזבח.

steps.title: The rule is only about animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's rule was said only about animal offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה taught this, it was talking about animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה's rule was never meant to include birds. It was only about animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'all קדשי מזבח' are narrowed to mean all animal offerings. Birds and מנחות were never part of the rule, so the other משנה does not contradict it.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal, meaning cattle, sheep or goats
When it taught: the case the משנה was talking about

phrases.english: When it taught this, it was about animals

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from birds
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the משנה's words
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule 'all קדשי מזבח' includes birds.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule is only about animal offerings, so birds are not a contradiction.

steps.title: The offspring of an altar animal makes no substitute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges again. The offspring of a sacrificial animal is a קדשי מזבח animal, yet another משנה says it does not make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the offspring is consecrated for the altar, and we learned that the offspring does not make a substitute!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second challenge. Even if we limit the rule to animals, there is an animal that does not make a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Limiting the rule to animals solved the problem of birds. But a ולד, the offspring of a consecrated animal, is itself an animal and is קדשי מזבח. Even so, a משנה says it does not make a תמורה. So the rule still seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: The offspring of a consecrated animal, which is holy by itself

phrases.english: But there is the offspring
it is consecrated for the altar
and we learned: the offspring does not make a substitute

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new challenge to the rule, even after it was limited to animals
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that all animal קדשי מזבח make a תמורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ולד is an animal and is קדשי מזבח, yet another משנה rules it does not make a תמורה.

steps.title: Our משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds that offspring does make a תמורה. The other משנה follows a different view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose view is this משנה? It is רבי יהודה, who says that offspring does make a substitute.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the problem by saying the two משניות follow different תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a מחלוקת about whether a ולד makes a תמורה. The משנה saying it does not follows one view. Our משנה, with its broad rule, follows רבי יהודה, who holds that it does. This is a different kind of answer from step 4: it does not reread our משנה, it assigns it to a particular תנא.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this? A way of assigning a teaching to a specific תנא

steps.whatToRemember: For now, the rule 'all קדשי מזבח make a תמורה' is limited to animals and is assigned to רבי יהודה, who includes the ולד. Step 9 will show this assignment is not needed.

phrases.english: Whose view is this?
It is רבי יהודה
who says: the offspring makes a substitute

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ולד
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to a specific תנא (a disagreement between תנאים)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both משניות follow the same view, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our משנה follows רבי יהודה, who holds that a ולד makes a תמורה. The other משנה follows the opposing view.

steps.title: A substitute itself does not make a substitute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה again: a תמורה is a קדשי מזבח animal, yet another משנה says a תמורה does not make a תמורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But look at a תמורה itself. It is holy for the מזבח, and yet we learned that a תמורה does not make another תמורה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third problem for the משנה's rule that every קדשי מזבח animal makes a תמורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמורה animal is truly holy for the מזבח. So if the rule were "all קדשי מזבח make a תמורה," a תמורה should make one too. But a משנה clearly says it does not, so the rule seems too broad.

keyTerms.meaning: A substitute: an animal someone tried to swap for a holy animal, which then becomes holy too
Things made holy to be brought on the altar
A substitute does not make another substitute

phrases.english: But there is a substitute itself,
which is consecrated for the altar,
and we learned: a substitute does not make a substitute!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the offspring problem was answered with רבי יהודה, a new counterexample is raised.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that all קדשי מזבח make a תמורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A תמורה is a holy animal for the מזבח, yet it does not make a תמורה, which contradicts the word "all".

steps.title: The rule speaks only about the main offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה's rule refers only to an animal that was made holy as an offering directly, not to one that became holy through another animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the משנה taught this rule, it was talking about the main offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 7 by narrowing the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule "all קדשי מזבח make a תמורה" covers only the עיקר זיבחא, an animal made holy directly as an offering. A תמורה only got its holiness from another animal, so it is not covered by the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The main offering: an animal made holy directly, not through another animal
When it was taught (introduces what the rule really refers to)

phrases.english: When it was taught,
it was about the main offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the challenge of step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule covers every animal that is holy for the מזבח, including a תמורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule covers only the main offering, so a תמורה is outside it.

steps.title: Now the משנה can follow the רבנן too
steps.stepSummary: Since the rule refers only to the main offering, the offspring problem disappears, and the משנה no longer has to follow רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Now that you have reached this idea, you can even say the משנה follows the רבנן, because the rule was taught only about the main offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the offspring problem from step 5 and gives it a better answer using the new idea from step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 the גמרא said the משנה follows רבי יהודה so the offspring could be explained. Now we see that the offspring, like a תמורה, is not a main offering, so it is not covered by the rule anyway. So the משנה can follow the רבנן too, who say offspring does not make a תמורה.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that you have come to this idea
You can even say
The Sages, the majority view

steps.whatToRemember: The rule "all קדשי מזבח make a תמורה" covers only the main offering. A תמורה and an offspring are not included, so the משנה works even according to the רבנן.
steps.confusionAlert: This does not take back step 6 as wrong. It just shows we no longer need to say the משנה follows only רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: Now that you have come to this,
phrases.notes: "This" means the answer just given, that the rule is only about the main offering.

phrases.english: you can even say it follows the Rabbis,
since when it was taught, it was about the main offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא דַאֲתֵית לְהָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer of step 8 to replace the answer of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Better answer that makes an earlier forced answer unnecessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה must follow רבי יהודה to fit the offspring case.
steps.terutzMaskana: The offspring is not a main offering, so the משנה can follow the רבנן as well.

steps.title: Why may craftsmen be paid from קדשי בדק הבית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that craftsmen are not paid from קדשי מזבח, and infers that they are paid from קדשי בדק הבית. It wants the source for this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says we do not pay the craftsmen from them. This implies that from קדשי בדק הבית we do pay them. Where do we learn that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and draws an inference from it. This sets up the next step, which will give the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only says craftsmen are not paid from קדשי מזבח. From this we learn that they may be paid from קדשי בדק הבית. The גמרא wants to know why holy money may be used for wages.

keyTerms.meaning: Craftsmen who work for the בית המקדש
Things made holy for the upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
This implies (introduces an inference from the משנה)

phrases.english: "And we do not give from them to the craftsmen," etc.
phrases.notes: "Them" means קדשי מזבח, the money set aside for altar offerings.

phrases.english: This implies that from Temple-upkeep holy things we do give?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תמורה topic and moves to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that craftsmen may be paid from קדשי בדק הבית

steps.title: "ועשו לי": build from what is Mine
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו learns from the פסוק "ועשו לי" that the משכן is built from holy property, so craftsmen may be paid from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: the פסוק says "and they shall make for Me," which means from what is Mine.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives the source for the inference in step 10.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "לי" (for Me) is read as "משלי" (from Mine). So the building work of the משכן is paid for from holy property, which means craftsmen's wages may come from קדשי בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק
"And they shall make for Me" (about building the משכן)
From what is Mine, meaning from holy property

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
for the verse says, "And they shall make for Me":
from what is Mine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "ועשו לי" teaches that the משכן is built from holy property, so craftsmen may be paid from it.

steps.title: Who holds that unspecified consecrations go to בדק הבית?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that unspecified consecrations go to בדק הבית and that בדק הבית holiness takes effect on everything, and asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said there are things in קדשי בדק הבית that are not in קדשי מזבח. The משנה said: unspecified consecrations go to בדק הבית, and its holiness takes effect on everything. Who is the תנא of this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last part of the משנה and asks whose opinion it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if someone makes something holy without saying for what, it goes to בדק הבית. The גמרא suspects this is not everyone's view, so it asks which תנא the משנה follows.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrations made without saying what they are for
It takes effect on everything
Who is the תנא? (Which sage's opinion is this?)

phrases.english: "There is in Temple-upkeep holy things," etc.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר מָר: סְתָם הֶקְדֵּשׁוֹת לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: The Master said: unspecified consecrations go to Temple upkeep,
phrases.notes: "The Master" here is just our משנה being quoted.

phrases.english: and it takes effect on everything.
Who is the tanna?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the last clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that unspecified consecrations go to בדק הבית

steps.title: The משנה does not follow רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says this part of the משנה does not follow רבי יהושע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: it is not like רבי יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 12 by saying whose view the משנה does not follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of naming who the משנה follows, רבי יוחנן names who it does not follow: רבי יהושע. This tells us רבי יהושע holds differently about unspecified consecrations, which the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: Not in line with (the view of a certain sage)

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba said
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
It is not like Rabbi Yehoshua.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה's rule about unspecified consecrations is not according to רבי יהושע.

steps.title: The source: רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע on altar-fit animals in consecrated property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a source in which רבי יהושע sends altar-fit males directly to the altar. This shows he does not hold that unspecified consecrations all go to בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: someone consecrated all his property, and it included animals fit for the altar, both males and females. רבי אליעזר says: sell the males to people who need עולות and sell the females to people who need שלמים. The money goes with the rest of the property to בדק הבית. רבי יהושע says: the males themselves are offered as עולות. The females are sold for שלמים, and with their money he buys עולות. The rest of the property goes to בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is backing up רבי יוחנן's statement from step 13. It quotes the source showing that רבי יהושע does not send unspecified consecrations to בדק הבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said unspecified consecrations go to בדק הבית. רבי אליעזר fits this, because in his view even the altar-fit animals end up as money for בדק הבית. רבי יהושע sends the males, and the money from the females, to the altar. So for him, a plain consecration of altar-fit animals is aimed at the altar, and the משנה cannot follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates all his property without saying what it is for
Burnt offerings, which must be male animals
Peace offerings, which may be male or female
And their money, meaning the money received from selling the animals
The Temple upkeep fund

steps.confusionAlert: Even רבי אליעזר does not waste the animals. They are still sold to people who need offerings. The argument is only about where the holiness and the money go: to בדק הבית or to the altar.

phrases.english: As it is taught: one who consecrates his property,
phrases.notes: He consecrated everything without saying what it is for. That is exactly the 'unspecified consecration' case from the משנה.

phrases.english: and among it there was an animal
fit for the altar,
males and females —
Rabbi Eliezer says:
the males are sold for the needs of burnt offerings,
and the females are sold for the needs of peace offerings,
and their money goes
with the rest of the property to Temple upkeep.
Rabbi Yehoshua says:
the males themselves are offered as burnt offerings,
and the females are sold for the needs of peace offerings
and he brings burnt offerings with their money,
and the rest of the property goes to Temple upkeep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבי יוחנן's claim in step 13
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהושע does not hold that unspecified consecrations automatically go to בדק הבית
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with the dispute between רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע about someone who consecrated property that included altar-fit animals
steps.whyThisMatters: This source is the basis for linking the משנה's rule to רבי אליעזר and not to רבי יהושע.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: with an all-male herd, even רבי אליעזר agrees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that רב אדא בר אהבה, quoting רב, reads the dispute differently. If the herd is all males, everyone agrees the animals go to the altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: This argues with רב אדא בר אהבה. רב אדא בר אהבה said in the name of רב: with a herd that is all males, even רבי אליעזר agrees, because a person does not pass up making altar offerings and consecrate instead to בדק הבית.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that רב reads the רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע dispute differently from the way it was just explained. This step gives the first half of his view: for an all-male herd, there is no dispute.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's approach treats רבי אליעזר as holding that unspecified consecrations go to בדק הבית even when the animals are altar-fit. רב says that is not true for an all-male herd. A person would surely prefer to give fit animals to the altar, so even רבי אליעזר makes them עולות. This means the dispute is not a general argument about where unspecified consecrations go.

keyTerms.meaning: It disagrees with another view
A herd or flock
Agrees
Things consecrated for the altar, meaning offerings
A person does not pass up something

phrases.english: And this disagrees with Rav Adda bar Ahava,
phrases.notes: 'This' is the way the dispute was just explained, as a general argument about where unspecified consecrations go.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: as Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav said:
with a herd that is entirely males,
even Rabbi Eliezer agrees,
phrases.notes: He agrees with רבי יהושע that the males are offered as עולות.

phrases.english: because a person does not pass up altar offerings
and consecrate to Temple upkeep instead.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רב reads the dispute just quoted in a different way
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In an all-male herd of altar-fit animals, even רבי אליעזר holds that an unspecified consecration goes to the altar

steps.title: The real dispute is a mixed herd: does a person split his vow?
steps.stepSummary: רב explains that they argue only about a half-male, half-female herd. רבי אליעזר holds that a person does not split one vow into two kinds of consecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue only about a herd that is half males and half females. רבי אליעזר holds that a person does not split his vow. Since the females cannot be עולות, the males are not עולות either.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב's explanation. It tells us exactly where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע argue and why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A mixed herd was consecrated with one statement. The females cannot be עולות, because a עולה must be male. רבי אליעזר says one vow is not split between two purposes, so the whole herd goes the same way, to בדק הבית. In רב's reading, the argument is about splitting a vow, not about the general rule for unspecified consecrations.

keyTerms.meaning: They argued only about this case
Half
A person does not split one vow into different kinds of consecration

steps.whatToRemember: There are two readings of the dispute. In רבי יוחנן's reading, רבי יהושע disagrees with the משנה's rule that unspecified consecrations go to בדק הבית. In רב's reading, everyone agrees an all-male herd goes to the altar. The argument is only about a mixed herd, and it turns on whether a person splits his vow.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Splitting the vow' does not mean breaking a promise. It means one act of consecration being carried out in two different ways: some animals to the altar and some to בדק הבית.

phrases.english: They disagree only

phrases.aramaic: בְּעֵדֶר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מֶחֱצָה זְכָרִים וּמֶחֱצָה נְקֵבוֹת,
phrases.english: about a herd that has half males and half females,
and Rabbi Eliezer holds:
a person does not divide his vow,
and since the females are not burnt offerings —
the males are also not burnt offerings.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּעֵדֶר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ מֶחֱצָה זְכָרִים וּמֶחֱצָה נְקֵבוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's statement by naming the case they argue about and רבי אליעזר's reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The dispute is only about a mixed herd. רבי אליעזר holds that a person does not split his vow, so since the females cannot be עולות, the males are not עולות either.

steps.title: רבי יהושע holds a person can split his vow
steps.stepSummary: Finishing רב's first explanation: רבי יהושע holds that a person does split one vow into different kinds of consecration.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע holds that a person divides his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes רב's first explanation by giving רבי יהושע's side. He disagrees with רבי אליעזר and holds that one vow can be split.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 16, רבי אליעזר said a person does not split his vow in a half-male, half-female herd. רבי יהושע says he does. So each animal goes to the kind of holiness that fits it best.

keyTerms.meaning: Splits his vow, so one act of consecrating sends different items to different kinds of holiness

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
a person divides his vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ סָבַר: חוֹלֵק אֶת נִדְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב's two-sided explanation begun in step 16 by stating רבי יהושע's opposing view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהושע, a person can split one vow between altar holiness and other holiness.

steps.title: Second version: if only animals were consecrated, everyone agrees they go to the altar
steps.stepSummary: A different version of רב's explanation: when only animals were consecrated, even רבי אליעזר agrees they go to the altar, because people don't give up altar-holiness for בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say it another way. רב אדא בר אהבה said in the name of רב: if a person consecrated only animals, even רבי אליעזר agrees they go to the altar. A person does not pass up altar-holiness and choose בדק הבית instead.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second version of רב's explanation. In this version, a case of only animals is not argued about at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the argument was about a mixed herd of males and females. Here, any herd of only animals, even a mixed one, goes to the altar according to everyone. The reason is that a person would not waste an animal that could go on the altar by giving it to Temple upkeep.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the same teaching
Holiness for the altar, meaning offerings
Upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
Agrees, admits the point

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In the first, the argument is about a half-male, half-female herd. In the second, all animals go to the altar according to everyone, and the argument is only when other property is included.

phrases.english: Some say it in another version:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: Rav Adda bar Ahava said that Rav said:
Where he consecrated only animals,
even Rabbi Eliezer agrees [they go to the altar],
because a person does not pass up altar-holiness
and consecrate for Temple upkeep instead.

steps.triggerLanguage: לִישָּׁנָא אַחְרִינָא אָמְרִי לַהּ, אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a rival version of רב's explanation that replaces the one in steps 15-17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When only animals are consecrated without saying what for, everyone agrees they go to the altar.

steps.title: Second version: they argue only when other property is included
steps.stepSummary: In the second version, the argument is only when animals were consecrated together with other property. רבי אליעזר says the vow can't be split, so everything goes to בדק הבית. רבי יהושע says it can be split.
steps.simpleTranslation: They argue only when there is other property along with the animals. רבי אליעזר holds that a person does not split his vow. Since the other property can't go to the altar, the animals don't go to the altar either. רבי יהושע holds that a person does split his vow.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the second version by saying exactly where רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע disagree: a case of animals together with other property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other property, like money or tools, can never go on the altar. רבי אליעזר says one vow must have one kind of holiness, so the animals follow the property to בדק הבית. רבי יהושע lets the vow split, so the animals go to the altar and the rest goes to בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: Other property, things that are not animals and can't be offerings
They argued only about... (narrows the argument to one case)
Since this is so... that is also so (reasoning from one item to the other)

steps.whatToRemember: Second version: animals alone go to the altar according to everyone. With other property, רבי אליעזר sends everything to בדק הבית because the vow can't be split. רבי יהושע splits it.

phrases.english: They argued only
where there is other property along with them,
and Rabbi Eliezer holds:
a person does not divide his vow,
so since the other property is not for altar-holiness,
the animals are also not for altar-holiness,
and Rabbi Yehoshua holds:
a person divides his vow.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁיֵּשׁ שְׁאָר נְכָסִים עִמָּהֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second version begun in step 18 by placing the argument in the case of animals together with other property.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With other property included, רבי אליעזר sends the animals to בדק הבית because a vow can't be split. רבי יהושע splits the vow.

steps.title: Testing the versions against רבי אליעזר's words about the rest of the property
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר's words, 'their money goes with the rest of the property to בדק הבית,' and notes that this wording fits the second version well. This sets up a challenge to the first version.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר said: 'And their money goes with the rest of the property to בדק הבית.' This makes sense according to the second version, which is why it says 'with the rest of the property to בדק הבית.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next move. It shows that רבי אליעזר's wording fits the second version, and it is about to ask how the first version can explain the same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר's words mention 'the rest of the property.' That matches the second version, where the argument is about a case with other property, and the animals go to בדק הבית along with it. The word 'בשלמא' signals that a 'but according to the first version...' challenge is coming next.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted, it works well for this side (sets up a challenge to the other side)
The latter version, the second version
Their money, the money from selling the animals
That is why it teaches it this way

phrases.english: "And their money shall go
phrases.notes: These are רבי אליעזר's own words from the משנה in שקלים that the גמרא is now testing.

phrases.english: with the rest of the property to Temple upkeep" —
Granted, according to the latter version,
that is why it teaches:
"with the rest of the property to Temple upkeep."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions of רב (steps 15-17 and 18-19) against רבי אליעזר's actual wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first version of רב's explanation (steps 15-17)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי אליעזר's mention of 'the rest of the property' fits a case with other property, which matches only the second version. That leaves the first version, which talks about animals alone, needing an explanation.

steps.title: Challenge to the first version from the משנה's wording
steps.stepSummary: If רבי אליעזר never splits a vow even when only animals were consecrated, the משנה should just say the money goes to בדק הבית, without mentioning 'the rest of the property.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the first version, the משנה should have said: 'They shall go to בדק הבית!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב's first version. The משנה's wording, 'with the rest of the property,' seems to point to the second version instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, the argument is about a herd of only animals, so there is no 'rest of the property' to mention. The words 'with the rest of the property' therefore seem out of place. The משנה should simply have said the money goes to בדק הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: The first version (of רב's explanation)
Let it teach / it should have said
Upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש

phrases.english: But according to the first version,
let it teach: 'They shall go to Temple upkeep'!
phrases.notes: He means: just that, without the extra words 'with the rest of the property.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the move begun in step 20: the wording fits the second version, so here is the problem for the first.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's first version (the argument is about animals alone)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה mentions 'the rest of the property,' which makes no sense if only animals were consecrated.

steps.title: A ברייתא really does say it that way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a ברייתא does teach the shorter wording, 'and their money shall go to בדק הבית,' which fits the first version.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches it this way: 'And their money shall go to בדק הבית.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the first version. It points to a ברייתא that uses exactly the wording the challenge wanted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version is not knocked out. A ברייתא gives the version of רבי אליעזר's words without 'the rest of the property,' and that matches a case of animals only. So the first version has a textual source too.

keyTerms.meaning: Their money (the value received when they are sold)
Shall go to / be given to
Also like this (introduces support)

steps.whatToRemember: Both versions of רב stay standing. The משנה's wording fits the second version, and a ברייתא's wording fits the first.

phrases.english: It is also taught this way (in a ברייתא):
'And their money shall go to Temple upkeep.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to a parallel source that has the expected wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first version has no textual support, since the משנה mentions other property.
steps.terutzMaskana: A ברייתא has the shorter wording, which supports the first version.

steps.title: What does 'takes effect on everything' come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line that consecration for בדק הבית takes effect on everything, and asks what extra item this is meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Consecration for בדק הבית takes effect on everything.' What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks what the word 'everything' adds. This sets up רבינא's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'everything' sounds extra, so the גמרא assumes it is there to include something we might have thought was not included.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecration (making something holy property)
Takes effect on everything
To include what?

phrases.aramaic: הֶקְדֵּשׁ בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת חָל עַל הַכֹּל.
phrases.english: Consecration for Temple upkeep takes effect on everything.
To include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic: explaining another phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra case the word 'everything' includes.

steps.title: It includes shavings and fallen leaves
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that 'everything' includes wood shavings and fallen leaves, which also become holy for בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It comes to include shavings and fallen leaves.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers the question: the word 'everything' teaches that even small leftover bits like shavings and leaves are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think such small, worthless bits are not covered by the consecration. The משנה's word 'everything' teaches that they are holy too.

keyTerms.meaning: Shavings / scrapings
Fallen leaves

phrases.english: Ravina said:
To include shavings and fallen leaves.
phrases.notes: These come from a tree that was consecrated for בדק הבית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 23.

steps.title: What does the rule about growths come to include?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's line about מעילה on growths and asks what this rule is meant to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And one is liable for מעילה on their growths.' What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the next line of the משנה, about מעילה on what consecrated things produce, and asks what it adds. This sets up רב פפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts בדק הבית, where growths carry מעילה, with things for the altar, where they do not. The גמרא wants to know which specific items this contrast is pointing to.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for מְעִילָה (misusing holy property)
Growths / by-products (what the item produces)

phrases.english: And one is liable for misuse of their growths.
To include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next phrase of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which items the rule about growths is pointing to.

steps.title: Milk and eggs of altar-holy animals
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the rule points to things with altar-holiness: milk of consecrated animals and eggs of pigeons. For these there is no מעילה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It comes to include, in קדושת מזבח, milk of consecrated animals and eggs of pigeons.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the משנה's contrast is about by-products like milk and eggs. When they come from animals holy for the altar, there is no מעילה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה says growths carry מעילה only for בדק הבית, the hidden point is that for altar animals they do not. רב פפא names the classic examples: milk from sacrificial animals and eggs from pigeons set aside as offerings.

keyTerms.meaning: Holiness for the altar (animals set aside as offerings)
Milk of consecrated animals
Eggs of pigeons (or turtledoves)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
To include, regarding altar-holiness,
phrases.notes: He means: to teach that with altar-holiness these items carry no מעילה.

phrases.english: milk of consecrated animals and eggs of pigeons.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְאֵתוֹיֵי בִּקְדוּשַּׁת מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Milk and eggs from altar-holy animals carry no מעילה.

steps.title: A ברייתא on milk and eggs: altar versus בדק הבית
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that milk of consecrated animals and pigeon eggs may not be used, but there is no מעילה for them, and this applies only to קדשי מזבח. For קדשי בדק הבית, there is מעילה for a chicken's eggs and a donkey's milk.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: Milk of consecrated animals and eggs of pigeons: one may not benefit from them, but there is no מעילה. When is this said? With קדשי מזבח. But with קדשי בדק הבית, if one consecrated a chicken, there is מעילה for its egg. If he consecrated a female donkey, there is מעילה for its milk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that backs up רב פפא's answer. It also shows the opposite rule for בדק הבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For altar animals, the milk and eggs are forbidden to use, but they do not carry the full penalty of מעילה. For בדק הבית items, the eggs and milk are themselves holy property, so using them is מעילה. This is exactly the contrast in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: One may not get benefit from them
In which case was this said? (limits the rule)
Things holy for the altar (offerings)
A chicken (hen)

steps.whatToRemember: Milk and eggs: forbidden but no מעילה when the animal is for the altar. Real מעילה when the animal is for בדק הבית.
steps.confusionAlert: 'No מעילה' does not mean you may use them. The ברייתא says clearly that one may not benefit from them. It only means the special penalty of מעילה does not apply.

phrases.english: As it is taught (in a ברייתא):
Milk of consecrated animals and eggs of pigeons:
one may not benefit from them, but there is no liability for misuse.
In what case is this said?
With things consecrated for the altar,
but with things consecrated for Temple upkeep:
if one consecrated a chicken, one is liable for misuse of its egg,
(if he consecrated) a female donkey, one is liable for misuse of its milk.
phrases.notes: The words 'if he consecrated' carry over from the chicken case.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to support רב פפא's answer.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that milk and eggs of altar-holy animals carry no מעילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on milk and eggs, which contrasts קדשי מזבח with קדשי בדק הבית
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a clear rule: by-products of animals for בדק הבית are fully holy, while by-products of altar animals are forbidden but without מעילה.

steps.title: Even the strict view limits מעילה to growths fit for the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that even the opinion holding there is מעילה on גידולי מזבח only means growths that can be offered on the altar. Milk and eggs cannot be offered, so there is no מעילה on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even according to the one who says there is מעילה on growths of altar-consecrated animals, that is only for growths that are fit for the altar. But growths that are not fit for the altar, like milk and eggs, have no מעילה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is showing that the ברייתא's ruling (no מעילה on milk and eggs of altar animals) fits every opinion, even the strictest one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known disagreement about whether growths of altar-holy things carry מעילה. The גמרא says the ruling about milk and eggs does not depend on that disagreement. Even the strict view only covers growths that can themselves be brought on the altar, like a calf born to a consecrated animal. Milk and eggs can never be offered, so no one says they carry מעילה.

keyTerms.meaning: One is liable for מעילה, meaning misusing consecrated property
Growths or by-products of things consecrated for the altar
That are fit to be offered on the altar
According to the one who says; refers to a known opinion

steps.whatToRemember: For קדשי מזבח, only growths that can themselves go on the altar could ever carry מעילה. Milk and eggs never can, so there is no מעילה on them by anyone's view. For קדשי בדק הבית, there is מעילה even on a chicken's eggs and a donkey's milk.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the milk and eggs are not holy at all. The ברייתא said you may not use them. The only point here is that there is no מעילה (no קרבן מעילה penalty) for using them.
steps.whyThisMatters: It makes the ruling on milk and eggs agreed by all, so it is not tied to the debate over גידולי הקדש.

phrases.english: And even according to the one who said
there is misuse liability for growths of altar-consecrated things,
this applies only to growths that are fit for the altar,
but growths that are not fit for the altar,
there is no misuse liability for them.
phrases.notes: These are the milk and pigeon eggs from the ברייתא in the previous step.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲפִילּוּ לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מוֹעֲלִין בְּגִידּוּלֵי מִזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the ברייתא's ruling of no מעילה on milk and eggs of altar animals holds even under the opinion that allows מעילה on altar growths.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Growths of altar-consecrated animals that are not themselves fit for the altar, like milk and eggs, carry no מעילה according to all opinions.
